newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Thin trade props up Korea premiums.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Thin trade props up Korea premiums.

text.p: Continued labour unrest in South Korea marred sentiment in the local market but premiums for global depositary receipts held up in thin London trade.
"The offers are getting higher and higher. Blue chip Samsung is just not a fair indication of how the market is," said one trader.
The HSBC James Capel Korean GDR Index JCAEI fell 2.38 points, 3.98 percent, to 58.78 points after the KOSPI index fell 16.54 points, 2.57 percent, to 626.87.

Premiums for GDRs remain strong, at 56.34 percent for the Capel Index, while individual stocks such as Pohang Iron and Steel are on 89 percent and Korea Mobile Telecom is on 121 percent, while Samsung, which is usually the most widely traded receipt was on 58 percent.

"There is not any stock out there and premiums have been strong for some time although I would not rule out any change in sentiment as the news out of Korea on the labour unrest is pretty bad," said a trader.
South Korean prosecutors and managers on Monday launched a legal action against labour union leaders to try to crush strikes by 190,000 workers over labour legislation.
"There is demand for the market out there and a lack of offers on the over the counter market for quality shares," said the trader.

Elsewhere, Indian GDRs ended little changed with the Capel index off 0.53 points at 69.21, a premium of 22.11 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 11.69 points or 0.36 percent to 3,252.31.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.56 points, 0.58 percent, at 95.28, a premium of 6.51 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 24.40 points, 0.36 percent, to 6,844.75.
